angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 674,829 km at 194.87 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.1315 +/- 0.0158 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 194.87 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.97 +/- 0.09 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-49 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 674,829 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.92 +/- 0.3 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-49 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5600 +/- 150 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-49 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-49 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-49.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.428, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-49 (pscomppars): spectral type G6 V, from Wyttenbach et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A..36W/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-49 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.23 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-49 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.05339, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-49 (pscomppars): age 11.9 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/ApJ/919/138/table1 (Rot. vel. & per. of hot Jupiter host stars), column Prot: 50 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/ApJ/919/138/table1 (Rot. vel. & per. of hot Jupiter host stars), column Prot: 50 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-49 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.9 km/s, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.97 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.917. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
